9:["$","p","1",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Boho</strong> (short for <em>bohemian</em>) is the design language of layered textures, organic materials, vintage finds, and a deliberate rejection of matching-set furniture. For a home office, boho delivers something most other aesthetics can't: a workspace that feels like a creative sanctuary rather than a corporate cubicle."}}]
a:["$","p","2",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"Three things distinguish a real boho home office from a generic one:"}}]
b:["$","ul","3",{"children":[["$","li","0",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Layered textures</strong> — woven rugs, macramé wall hangings, jute baskets, woven accent pillows, raw wood. Multiple textures stacked rather than smooth surfaces everywhere."}}],["$","li","1",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Plants — lots of them</strong> — boho is the only aesthetic where 5-10 plants in a single room reads correct rather than cluttered. Trailing pothos, hanging spider plants, fiddle leaf figs, snake plants, succulents."}}],["$","li","2",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Vintage and handmade pieces</strong> — at least one antique item, one handmade item, and one item from your travels (or that looks like it). Mass-produced \"boho\" decor sets read fake instantly."}}]]}]

34:["$","h2","44",{"id":"common-mistakes","children":"Common Mistakes"}]
35:["$","ul","45",{"children":[["$","li","0",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Buying a \"boho decor set\" off Amazon.</strong> Mass-produced matching boho pieces read instantly fake. Boho lives on mismatch."}}],["$","li","1",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Plants in plastic pots.</strong> Use terracotta, ceramic, woven baskets, or stoneware. Plastic kills the look."}}],["$","li","2",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Too much color.</strong> Boho is earth tones + ONE saturated accent (rust OR dusty pink OR olive — pick one). Multiple bright colors stop reading as boho and start reading as chaotic."}}],["$","li","3",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Modern furniture with no texture.</strong> A sleek IKEA white desk doesn't become boho just by adding plants. The desk itself needs visible grain, vintage character, or natural finish."}}],["$","li","4",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Forgetting the rug.</strong> Boho lives on layered textures, and a rug is the most impactful texture in the room. Skipping it leaves the aesthetic flat."}}]]}]
36:["$","h2","46",{"id":"common-mistakes-specific-to-plants","children":"Common Mistakes Specific to Plants"}]
37:["$","ul","47",{"children":[["$","li","0",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Don't buy plants you can't keep alive.</strong> Sansevieria, pothos, ZZ plants, and snake plants are nearly indestructible. Calatheas and ferns will die in a week without specific care."}}],["$","li","1",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>One large statement plant beats 10 small struggling ones.</strong> A single 6-foot fiddle leaf or rubber plant in a beautiful terracotta pot creates more impact than 10 small succulents on a windowsill."}}],["$","li","2",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Group plants in odd numbers.</strong> Three plants on a shelf reads designed; four reads symmetrical and boring."}}]]}]

3b:["$","p","51",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>How is boho different from \"cottagecore\"?</strong>"}}]
3c:["$","p","52",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"Boho leans more global/eclectic with travel-inspired pieces, vintage finds, and layered patterns. Cottagecore is more pastoral/European with floral patterns, antique milk glass, and rural charm. Significant overlap but different sources of inspiration."}}]
